subject: Service exceptions / procurement path — exhibit language and evidence request
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clinivue.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clinivue.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood exhibit — request for exceptions & supporting evidence

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement needs to understand a few things before we can move the MSA/MSO to our legal team: specifically any availability carve-outs you require (planned maintenance windows, latency windows during model upgrades), plus the language you would like to see in an exhibit or order form that documents those exceptions.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you provide draft exhibit/order-form language we can insert into our MSA?
- We need uptime history (past 12 months) and a short description of your maintenance cadence/runbook for planned maintenance.

I'll attach a copy of our redlined MSA to this thread for reference. If it's easier, a short follow-up call with procurement + legal would work — we have slots Thursday afternoon.

Attachments: Clinivue_MSA_Redwood_v1.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

Thanks,
Sara Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
Clinivue Health
[sara.bennett@clinivue.com]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clinivue.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood exhibit — request for exceptions & supporting evidence

Sara — thanks for the note and the attached MSA. Looping in Karthik (sales engineering) and Priyom (contracts) to propose concrete exhibit text and the evidence package.

High-level options we typically offer for enterprise MSA customers (we can pick one or combine):
- Dedicated (reserved) pools: 99.9% monthly uptime SLA; limited planned-maintenance windows (we propose 3x 2-hour windows / quarter) that are excluded from uptime calculations.
- Hosted API: 99.5% monthly uptime SLA with a standard maintenance window (2 hours / month) excluded.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency guarantees depend on model/sequence length — we provide model/region profiles in the exhibit rather than a blanket per-token SLA.

We'll prepare: (1) draft exhibit that inserts a clear definition of "planned maintenance" and an exception clause, (2) an order-form snippet that ties the SLA variant to the product SKU, and (3) a 12-month uptime summary + one-page runbook.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll share draft Exhibit + order form today.
2) If you want alternative windows (e.g., longer maintenance blackout for major upgrades), say so and we'll provide language.
3) If procurement agrees, we can push the draft into DocuSign and include the exhibit as an addendum to the MSA.

I'll attach the draft exhibit and order-form snippet for initial review.

Attachments: draft_exhibit_service-exceptions.docx, orderform_snippet.txt, uptime_history_summary.csv

—
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clinivue.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 13:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood exhibit — request for exceptions & supporting evidence

Sara / Mateo — attaching suggested exhibit language below as plain text for easy cut/paste into Clinivue's MSA. This is intentionally modular so legal can accept or tweak sections without redoing the whole doc.

[BEGIN EXHIBIT — SERVICE AVAILABILITY AND EXCEPTIONS]
1. Definitions
  a. "Planned Maintenance": maintenance events scheduled at least 72 hours in advance and communicated to the customer. Planned Maintenance windows shall not exceed 6 hours per calendar month, unless mutually agreed.
  b. "Unavoidable Exception": events outside Redwood's reasonable control including provider outages, DDoS, force majeure, and customer-caused disruptions.

2. Uptime SLA
  a. For Dedicated capacity subscriptions, Redwood guarantees 99.9% Monthly Uptime. For Hosted API subscriptions, Redwood guarantees 99.5% Monthly Uptime.
  b. Monthly Uptime calculations exclude Planned Maintenance windows and any Unavoidable Exceptions.

3. Latency SLOs
  a. Redwood will provide per-model, per-region SLO profiles (e.g., 95th percentile request latency for supported sequence lengths). These profiles are referenced in the order form; latency is provided as informational SLOs and not a financially-backed credit unless explicitly stated in the order form.

4. Remedies and Credits
  a. For breaches of the Monthly Uptime SLA (excluding Planned Maintenance and Unavoidable Exceptions), customer remedies are limited to the credit schedule in the order form. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy.

5. Operational Evidence
  a. Redwood will provide a 12-month uptime summary and runbook upon request and during procurement. Production runbook includes maintenance cadence, notification process, and rollback procedures.
[END EXHIBIT]

Karthik — happy to discuss any tightening of the Planned Maintenance definition; these numbers reflect what we can reliably commit to across regions.

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clinivue.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clinivue.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood exhibit — request for exceptions & supporting evidence

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the exhibit language — this is helpful. A few clarifications from legal/procurement:
- Planned Maintenance: can we expand notification to 7 days where feasible? Procurement prefers longer notice where operationally possible.
- Latency SLOs: we appreciate per-model profiles; we need at least one example profile for the models we expect to use (long-form summarization and chat assistant). Can you include an example 95th percentile latency for 2k-token requests?
- Evidence: please include the 12-month uptime summary (CSV) and a one-page runbook PDF. Also add a short blurb describing regional fallbacks and multi-region replication behavior.

I attached a short list of additional questions in Clinivue_questions.csv. If everything looks good we will route the exhibit back to legal with a suggested edit to the Planned Maintenance notice period.

Attachments: clinivue_questions.csv

Best,
Sara

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@clinivue.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood exhibit — request for exceptions & supporting evidence

Sara — appreciated. We can do the following to close the loop quickly:
- Change Planned Maintenance notification to "at least 7 days when operationally possible; in emergency cases 72 hours" (we'll call out exceptions).
- Include an example latency profile for the two models you mentioned: 95th pct for 2k-token requests — Hosted API: ~1.4s per token batch (95th); Dedicated: ~0.35s per token batch (95th) — we will provide formal profiling numbers in the model-profile doc.
- Attached: uptime_history_summary.csv (12 months) and a short runbook summary (one-pager included in the Drive link).

If those changes work, we'll push the exhibit into DocuSign and send the signing link to procurement. Proposed DocuSign link below for reference — we'll create the envelope once you confirm the final exhibit language.

DocuSign (preview): https://app.docusign.com/CLV-Redwood-Exhibit
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cExhibitDraft

Mateo
